trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up, right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going around the edge to (1,5), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes around the edge to (5,1).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (up from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try right.
The line must go right: up is number 8, which comes later; down is number 9, which comes later.
Going down, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,5). So the line goes up.
Going around the edge to (5,3) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
The line must go down: right is number 7, which comes later.
Going right would force the line onto number 7 before its turn; going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 4. So the line goes left.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,3). So the line goes down.
Going left would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes right.
The line must go up: right is number 10, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (4,1), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,1). So the line goes up.
Going around the edge to (3,1) would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going around the edge to (5,1) would wall in number 10, the last number. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (5,2).
Going left would wall in number 10, the last number. So the line goes up.
Going left would leave both cell (3,1) and cell (5,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 2 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 25/25 cells (100%).
Generation 0: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Jackpot! A future after going right covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 25 cells x 25 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 1,440 variables and 3,918 clauses in 0.00 s (425 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.00 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
